'''Stephon Javonte Castle''' (born November 1, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]], winning a [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship]] in 2024. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class. Selected fourth overall by the Spurs in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Castle was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] for the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]]. In 2026, he reached the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] with the team.

==Early life and high school career==
Castle grew up in [[Covington, Georgia]], and attended [[Newton High School (Georgia)|Newton High School]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Hubbard |first=Phillip B. |date=August 22, 2022 |title=Newton basketball star Stephon Castle celebrated across Newton County for gold medal |url=https://www.covnews.com/sports/newton/newton-basketball-star-stephon-castle-celebrated-across-newton-county-gold-medal/ |access-date=June 19, 2023 |work=[[The Covington News]]}}</ref>
As a sophomore, he helped the Rams reach the 7A state quarterfinals, averaging 13.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 2.3 steals per game while shooting 41% from 3.<ref>{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=April 15, 2021 |title=2020-21 MaxPreps Sophomore All-America Team: D.J. Wagner headlines high school basketball's best from the Class of 2023|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/t2nUshVwNEqz2EQv12X2YA/2020-21-maxpreps-sophomore-all-america-team-dj-wagner-headlines-high-school-basketballs-best-from-the-class-of-2023.htm |access-date=April 28, 2026 |work=[[MaxPreps.com]]}}</ref>
He averaged 16.6 points, 6.5 rebounds, and 3.2 assists per game as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/2022/04/23/experts-break-down-the-game-of-uconn-mens-basketball-2023-commit-stephon-castle/|title=Experts break down the game of UConn men's basketball 2023 commit Stephon Castle|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=April 23, 2022|access-date=June 12, 2023}}</ref> 
He finished his senior year averaging 20.1 points, 9.5 rebounds, 4.8 assists, three steals, and two blocks per game to carry the Rams to the Class 7A state quarterfinals.<ref>{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=March 29, 2023 |title=2022-23 MaxPreps All-America Team: Cameron Boozer of Columbus headlines high school basketball's best |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/SxUDpqUOuUW4VE3APSX7fw/2022-23-maxpreps-all-america-team-cameron-boozer-of-columbus-headlines-high-school-basketballs-best.htm |access-date=August 5, 2023 |work=[[MaxPreps.com]]}}</ref>
Castle was selected to play in the [[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 25, 2023 |title=UConn men signee Castle named McDonald's All-American |url=https://www.journalinquirer.com/sports/college/uconn_mens_basketball/uconn-men-signee-castle-named-mcdonalds-all-american/article_04c2c3f8-9c82-11ed-a213-87684c7aba56.html |url-status=dead |access-date=June 12, 2023 |work=[[Journal Inquirer]] |archive-date=February 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230207042517/https://www.journalinquirer.com/sports/college/uconn_mens_basketball/uconn-men-signee-castle-named-mcdonalds-all-american/article_04c2c3f8-9c82-11ed-a213-87684c7aba56.html }}</ref>

===Recruiting===
Castle was initially rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by most recruiting services. On November 19, 2021, he committed to playing college basketball for [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] during his junior year over offers from [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], and [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/2021/11/19/class-of-2023-four-star-guard-stephon-castle-commits-to-uconn-mens-basketball/|title=Class of 2023 four-star guard Stephon Castle commits to UConn men's basketball|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=November 19, 2021|access-date=May 14, 2023}}</ref> By the end of his senior year Castle had been re-rated as a five-star recruit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://connecticut.rivals.com/news/stephon-castle-freshman-introduction|title=UConn Hoops Freshmen Intros -- Five-Star G Stephon Castle|first=Stratton|last=Stave|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=May 10, 2023|access-date=May 14, 2023|archive-date=May 14, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230514191100/https://connecticut.rivals.com/news/stephon-castle-freshman-introduction|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/high-school-notebook-stephon-castle-is-on-the-rise|title=High School Notebook: Stephon Castle is on the Rise|first=Ignacio|last=Rissotto|website=[[SI.com]]|date=March 3, 2023|access-date=June 19, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
Castle enrolled at [[UConn]] in June 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ctpost.com/sports/uconn-womens-basketball/article/uconn-mens-basketball-dan-hurley-kk-arnold-18128140.php |title=UConn freshmen basketball players have arrived in Storrs: KK Arnold, Stephon Castle, and more|first=Christine|last=Butterfield|work=Connecticut Post|date=June 1, 2023|access-date=June 8, 2023}}</ref> He helped lead the UConn Huskies to win the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2024 NCAA national championship]]. He declared for the [[2024 NBA draft]] on April 19, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Leahy |first=Sean |date=April 19, 2024 |title=UConn freshman guard Stephon Castle declares for 2024 NBA Draft |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/uconn-freshman-guard-stephon-castle-declares-for-2024-nba-draft-150452729.html |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=Yahoo! Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===San Antonio Spurs (2024–present)===
====Rookie of the Year (2024–2025)====
On June 26, 2024, Castle was selected with the fourth overall pick by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Peter|last=Sampson|title=Victor Wembanyama’s first message to Spurs’ Stephon Castle after NBA Draft|url=https://clutchpoints.com/spurs-news-victor-wembanyama-message-stephon-castle-nba-draft|website=ClutchPoints|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=June 26, 2024}}</ref> and on July 2, he signed with the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Spurs Sign Stephon Castle To Rookie Scale Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/spurs-sign-stephon-castle-to-rookie-scale-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 2, 2024|access-date=July 2, 2024}}</ref> He made his [[2024 NBA Summer League|NBA Summer League]] debut on July 6, putting up 12 points, six rebounds, and three assists in a 97–65 loss to the [[2024–25 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/spurs-news-stephon-castle-ruled-out-nba-summer-league-minor-injury-scare|title=Spurs' Stephon Castle ruled out for NBA Summer League after injury scare|website=ClutchPoints|last=Ledesma|first=Hector|date=July 15, 2024|access-date=July 19, 2024}}</ref>

====First Finals appearance (2025–2026)====
On November 12, 2025, Castle recorded his first career triple-double with 23 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in the Spurs’ 125–120 loss to the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]]. He and [[Victor Wembanyama]] became the first pair of teammates in Spurs history to record triple-doubles in the same game. They also became the fifth duo in NBA history to each produce a 20-point triple-double in a game.<ref>{{cite web |date=13 November 2025 |title=Wemby, Castle proud despite dual triple-doubles in Spurs loss |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401810075 |access-date=13 November 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On February 7, 2026, Castle put up his second career triple-double with a career-high 40 points, alongside 12 rebounds and 12 assists, on 15-of-19 shooting from the field, in a 138–125 win over the [[2025–26 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]]. With the performance, he became only the second player in Spurs franchise history after [[David Robinson]] to record a 40-point triple-double.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/spurs-news-stephon-castle-joins-elite-san-antonio-company-career-best-performance-mavericks|title=Spurs’ Stephon Castle joins elite San Antonio company with career-best performance vs. Mavericks|website=ClutchPoints|last=Imran|first=Abdullah|date=February 7, 2026|access-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/texas/news/spurs-stephon-castle-40-point-triple-double-vs-mavericks/|title=Castle drops 40-point triple-double as Spurs beat Mavericks again|website=CBS Sports|date=February 7, 2026|access-date=February 7, 2026}}</ref> On March 12, Castle put up his third career triple-double with 30 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 136–131 loss to the [[2025–26 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/spurs-news-stephon-castle-victor-wembanyama-club-stats-nuggets|title=Spurs’ Stephon Castle joins Victor Wembanyama club with bonkers stats vs. Nuggets|website=ClutchPoints|last=Mariano|first=Paolo|date=March 12, 2026|access-date=March 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-stephon-castle-tallies-third-triple-double/|title=Spurs' Stephon Castle: Tallies third triple-double|website=CBS Sports|date=March 12, 2026|access-date=March 13, 2026}}</ref> On March 28, Castle recorded his fourth career triple-double with 22 points, 10 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 127–95 win over the [[2025–26 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Stephon Castle gets triple-double as Spurs trounce Bucks 127-95 for eighth straight win |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810931 |website=ESPN.com  |date=March 28, 2026 |access-date=March 28, 2026}}</ref> 

On April 24, in Game 3 of the [[2026 NBA playoffs#(2) San_Antonio Spurs vs. (7) Portland Trail Blazers|Western Conference First Round]] against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], Castle put up 33 points and five assists in a 120–108 win. His teammate [[Dylan Harper]] put up 27 points, as they joined [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Russell Westbrook]] as the only duos to each put up 25 points in the same playoff game at 21 years old or younger in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/san-antonio-spurs/spurs-news-dylan-harper-stephon-castle-game-3-heroics-kd-westbrook|title=Spurs guards Dylan Harper, Stephon Castle’s Game 3 heroics join Kevin Durant, Russell Westbrook company|website=ClutchPoints|last=Davis|first=Josh|date=April 25, 2026|access-date=April 27, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7228272/2026/04/25/spurs-blazers-nba-playoffs-game-3-dylan-harper-carter-bryant/|title=Carter Bryant, Dylan Harper take over Spurs’ comeback win in moment they dreamed of|website=The Athletic|last=Weiss|first=Jared|date=April 25, 2026|access-date=April 27, 2026}}</ref> On June 8, in Game 3 of the [[NBA Finals]], Castle helped the Spurs cut the series deficit to 2–1 by recording 23 points, five rebounds, five assists, one steal, and one block in a 115–111 victory over the [[New York Knicks]], snapping the Knicks’ 13-game winning streak.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA Finals: Spurs bounce back from Game 2 disaster, silence Madison Square Garden in Game 3 thriller over Knicks|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/live/spurs-vs-knicks-score-live-updates-game-3-victor-wembanyama-jalen-brunson-stats-box-score-president-donald-trump-213000599.html|website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=June 8, 2026|access-date=June 9, 2026}}</ref> The Spurs ultimately lost the series 4–1 to the Knicks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship, defeating Spurs in five games|website=NBA.com|last=Lambert|first=Ben|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
Castle played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States under-18 basketball team]] at the [[2022 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.courant.com/2022/06/03/uconn-mens-basketball-commit-stephon-castle-named-to-usa-basketball-mens-u18-roster/|title=UConn men's basketball commit Stephon Castle named to USA Basketball men's U18 roster|work=[[Hartford Courant]]|date=June 3, 2022|access-date=June 8, 2023}}</ref> He averaged 5.5 points and 2.2 rebounds per game as the United States won the gold medal.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hubbard |first=Phillip B. |date=June 15, 2022 |title=USA BASKETBALL: Castle, Team USA take gold |url=https://www.covnews.com/sports/newton/usa-basketball-castle-team-usa-take-gold/ |access-date=June 8, 2023 |work=[[The Covington News]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Castle is the son of Quannette and Stacey Castle. He has a younger sister, Staci, and an older brother, Quenton.<ref>{{cite web |title=Stephon Castle - Men's Basketball |url=https://uconnhuskies.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/stephon-castle/13286 |website=University of Connecticut Athletics |access-date=26 July 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Castle's father, Stacey, was a teammate with [[NBA Hall of Famer]] [[Tim Duncan]] at [[Wake Forest University]] during the [[1993–94 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|1993–94 season]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Duarte |first=Jeph |date=June 30, 2024 |title=Stephon Castle’s curious tie to Tim Duncan |url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/2024/6/30/24189076/stephon-castle-stacey-castle-curious-tie-to-tim-duncan-nba-san-antonio-spurs-wake-forest-aau-draft |work=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref>
